instructions: Put the potatoes in a large pot, cover them with cold water by about an inch, and add 2 teaspoons of the salt.
Bring the pot to a boil over high heat, then turn it down to a steady simmer. Cook the potatoes for 15 to 20 minutes, until a fork slides in easily.
Meanwhile, set the oven rack about 6 inches under the broiler and turn the broiler on high.

In a large salad bowl, whisk the Dijon and the vinegar. Slowly whisk in the olive oil until it thickens a little, then stir in the remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt and the pepper. Put the greens on top and leave them untossed for now.
Drain the potatoes and let them steam dry for 2 minutes. Halve them and lay them cut side up in a single layer on two rimmed baking sheets.
Cover each potato half with a slice of cheese, using half the cheese on each sheet.
Broil the first sheet for 3 to 4 minutes, until the cheese is bubbling and spotted brown. Stay close. Broilers vary, and the cheese goes from brown to burnt fast.
Transfer the first sheet to the table, then slide the second sheet under the broiler for 3 to 4 minutes.
Toss the salad with its dressing. Put the cornichons and pickled onions in small bowls. Serve the potatoes hot with the pickles and the salad.
method_notes: Lead is Christina's Cucina (raclette potatoes with cornichons, 4.9 from 26), which uses no raclette grill: boiled potatoes, cheese melted under the broiler, cornichons. It is written as an appetizer for two, so the amounts here are scaled up to a dinner (about 4 oz of cheese a person). The pickled onions and mustard salad come from Obviously French's family raclette dinner; Good Cheap Eats adds ham, which is left out here. Naturally gluten-free and nut-free.
